review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: Fit a linear slope to the bioluminescence signal during the rotation-ON phase
errors.issue: A slope of intensity reports change in ATP concentration, not synthesis flux when luciferase consumes ATP. The separately proposed intensity integration also needs a calibrated photon-yield/impulse response, including signal after the drive interval. The late consumption caveat does not supply that analysis.

errors.quote: corresponding to at most 3 pre-bound nucleotides per F1
errors.issue: Three catalytic sites are not a validated upper bound on all initial ATP in enzyme, noncatalytic binding sites, inactive protein, surfaces and reagents. Measure the complete initial pool; exceeding 3 times an active-motor count cannot categorically rule out release.

errors.quote: In a separate optical setup, confirm that magnetic beads attached to gamma subunits rotate
errors.issue: A separate validation cannot establish actual rotation/slip in each chemical assay interval. Record trajectories during chemistry or use a validated contemporaneous census; prescribed frequency alone is insufficient.

errors.quote: From known bead geometry, viscous drag coefficient, and rotation speed, estimate applied torque.
errors.issue: Viscous drag alone omits the enzyme load and near-surface/linkage effects. A published stall torque is not the transmitted torque in this setup; use an independently calibrated actuator and work balance.

Removing ADP and phosphate together does not isolate phosphate dependence or distinguish ADP disproportionation. Add separate omissions with matched ionic conditions and nucleotide-product mass balance.

errors.quote: All experimental conditions will be labeled with this convention.
errors.issue: A declared CW/CCW convention and literature direction need an empirical same-geometry hydrolysis reference plus an orientation census. The proposed verification checks the prescribed direction without establishing this mapping.

rationale: Relevant substrate, enzyme and direction controls with independent preparations and numerical settings recognizable as proposals. Central ATP-rate conversion, bound-pool threshold and actual-motion/torque validation remain flawed. The correct reverse-coupling hypothesis and predicted substrate-dependent outcome earn matching credit; the readout component remains partial.
reference_guardrails: The packet establishes ATP-associated directional motion, not an ATP-per-turn yield, torque, universal camera sign or completed reverse-synthesis experiment. Proposed numerical settings may earn credit when explicitly qualified.
Correct the draft reference by explicitly requiring magnesium/cofactor and nucleotide speciation qualification; its generic reaction inventory is not a complete buffer recipe.
Reverse operation should generate new ATP repeatedly beyond measured initial available/bound pools. Three catalytic sites are not a universal total ATP-contamination bound.

Luciferase is an acceptable chemical readout when its consumption, recovery and time response are calibrated. An intensity slope is not generally synthesis flux; chromatographic detection is an alternative, not mandatory.
Label incorporation can reflect exchange. Pair isotope provenance with net-product/material balance; account for reporter consumption and sample removal as appropriate.
Empirical direction, mixed surface orientations, actual rotor turns and transmitted torque are distinct quantities. Do not replace any with the nominal actuator command.

Mechanical input can drive ATP synthesis uphill. Low initial ATP may aid sensitivity but does not prove positive chemical-energy storage; energetic efficiency needs both work and chemical free energy.

ATP per turn is a coupling yield, not energetic efficiency. Inactive fractions, orientation, incomplete entrainment and analytical recovery can reduce apparent yield without establishing loose molecular coupling.
Separate ADP and phosphate controls help discriminate intended synthesis from alternative ATP production. Inhibitor effects require assay and enzyme specificity validation.

Matching is retrospective and applies all five predeclared components. A partially correct historical direction is recorded even when the experimental design is flawed; no claim of prospective novelty or uncontaminated holdout is made.

review_sources.title: Itoh et al. (2004): mechanically driven ATP synthesis by F1-ATPase
review_sources.scope: Reviewer read main text, figure captions and Methods. Supports the reverse-rotation historical target, with documented orientation and reporter-response limitations. Supplements and numerical reanalysis remain unaudited; not provided to candidates.
